questionBank.title: Object-Oriented Programming — Week 1 Question Bank
questionBank.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questionBank.syllabusCoverage: Structured Programming vs Object-Oriented Programming; Procedures, Control Structures, and Shared Data; Objects, Classes, State, and Behavior.

questions.question: What is the main idea of structured programming?

options.A: Organizing a program into clear control structures and procedures
options.B: Representing every program element as an object

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Structured programming organizes code into top-down procedures and fundamental control structures.

questions.question: Which set contains the fundamental control structures commonly associated with structured programming?

options.A: Sequence, selection, and iteration

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Sequence, selection (decision/if-else), and iteration (loops) are the three pillars of structured programming.

questions.question: In structured programming, a large problem is commonly divided into:

options.A: Smaller procedures or functions

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Procedural decomposition breaks a large program down into manageable functions.

questions.question: What is a major focus of structured programming?

options.A: The sequence of operations and procedures used to solve a problem
options.B: The identity of every real-world object

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Focus is placed on algorithm step sequences and procedure calls.

questions.question: Why can structured programs become difficult to manage as a system grows in size and complexity?

options.A: Large numbers of procedures and shared data can create complex dependencies

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Global state and procedural cross-dependencies lead to high coupling as system size grows.

questions.question: Which issue can arise when data is widely shared among many procedures?

options.A: Changes to data can affect multiple parts of the program

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Unprotected shared data means a change in one place can inadvertently break unrelated procedures.

questions.question: A major challenge in modeling complex real-world systems is:

options.A: Managing many entities, their states, behaviors, and relationships

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Real-world systems comprise numerous entities whose states and behaviors continuously interact.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the object-oriented programming paradigm?

options.A: Modeling a system using interacting objects that combine data and behavior

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — OOP encapsulates data (attributes) and code (methods) together into objects.

questions.question: In object-oriented programming, an object generally represents:

options.A: An entity with state and behavior

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — An object has identity, state (data), and behavior (methods).

questions.question: What is a class in object-oriented programming?

options.A: A blueprint or user-defined type for creating objects
options.B: A single object stored in memory

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — A class defines the structure and behavior pattern that its instances (objects) possess.

questions.question: If Student is a class, which is an example of an object?

options.A: student1

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — student1 is an individual instantiated object of class Student.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a class from an object?

options.A: A class is a definition or blueprint; an object is an instance of that class
options.B: A class is always an object in memory
options.C: An object defines the class structure
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Class = blueprint / type; Object = concrete instance in memory.

questions.question: In an OOP class, data members primarily represent:

options.A: The state or characteristics of an object

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Data members / fields represent attributes and internal state.

questions.question: In an OOP class, methods primarily represent:

options.A: Behavior or operations performed by an object

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Methods represent actions, behaviors, and operations on an object's state.

questions.question: In a banking system, which is the most appropriate candidate for a class?

options.A: BankAccount

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — BankAccount is a domain entity, while deposit() is a method and balance is an attribute.

questions.question: For a Student class, which combination correctly represents state and behavior?

options.A: name and rollNo as state; display() as behavior
options.B: display() as state; name as behavior
options.C: Student as state; class as behavior
options.D: compiler as state; memory as behavior

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Attributes name and rollNo define state, while display() is an action (behavior).

questions.question: Why can object-oriented modeling be useful for complex real-world systems?

options.A: It can represent entities, their responsibilities, and relationships in a structured way
options.B: It eliminates the need for algorithms
options.D: It removes the need for data

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — OOP aligns programmatic design closely with real-world entities and responsibilities.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a key difference between structured programming and OOP?

options.A: Structured programming emphasizes procedures and control flow, while OOP emphasizes objects combining state and behavior
options.B: Structured programming uses code, while OOP does not

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Procedural paradigm focuses on algorithmic steps, whereas OOP centers on interacting objects.

questions.question: Which statement about objects created from the same class is correct?

options.A: They can have different values for their non-static data members
options.B: They must always contain identical data
options.C: Only one object can ever be created from a class

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Each object instance holds its own distinct member values (state).

questions.question: Which sequence best represents the basic transition from a real-world problem to an object-oriented model?

options.A: Identify relevant entities → represent them as classes/objects → define state and behavior
options.B: Compile code → identify entities → write requirements
options.C: Create database tables → remove classes → define objects
options.D: Write random functions → deploy → identify the problem

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A — Analysis identifies entities; design maps them into classes with attributes and methods.
